title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Singapore net-zero emissions targets
sections.summary: Singapore announced plans for net-zero by 2050, around 60 MtCO2e in 2030, and 45 to 50 MtCO2e by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2022, the Government announced its plans to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It aimed to reduce Singapore's emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, the Government announced that it will reduce emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2035.

sections.label: Singapore electricity production sources
sections.summary: 95% of Singapore's electricity production comes from liquefied natural gas, with the rest from oil, coal, solar and waste.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, 95% of Singapore's electricity production comes from liquefied natural gas (LNG) and the remaining is dependent on oil, coal, solar and waste supply.

sections.label: AI energy consumption comparisons
sections.summary: AI queries and image generation use far more energy than Google searches, light bulbs, smartphone charging, or smaller task-specific models.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To put things in perspective, just one query with ChatGPT uses up to 10 times as much energy as a Google search query, enough to power a light bulb for 20 minutes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Generating a single image using an AI model can take as much energy as fully charging a smartphone, thousands of times more energy-intensive than generating text.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Using large general-purpose models, such as large language models like ChatGPT can consume up to 30 times more energy than a smaller model created specifically for the task.

sections.label: Singapore 2035 emissions commitment
sections.summary: In February this year, Singapore committed to reduce emissions to between 45 and 50 MtCO2e in 2035.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In February this year, Singapore committed itself to reduce emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e) in 2035.

sections.label: Singapore 2035 NDC submission
sections.summary: Singapore's recent 2035 NDC submission targets reducing emissions to 45 to 50 million tonnes by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Singapore's recent submission on our 2035 NDCs states that we target to reduce our emission to 45 to 50 million tonnes by 2035.

sections.label: Singapore emissions abatement effort
sections.summary: Achieving 15 million tonnes of abatement would require halving industry emissions or cutting power sector emissions by around 70%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: To put it in perspective, to achieve 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide abatement from today's emission level, Singapore would need to either halve our primary emissions from the industry sector or reduce the emissions from our power sector by around 70%.

sections.label: Green electricity import carbon abatement
sections.summary: NUS Energy Studies Institute preliminary estimation says importing an additional four gigawatts of green electricity could abate about 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Based on preliminary estimation by the Energy Studies Institute at the National University of Singapore (NUS), importing an additional four gigawatts of green electricity could abate about 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

sections.label: Cross-border discussions status update
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government can update on the status of cross-border discussions and whether they progress as expected and align with infrastructure plans and timelines.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Will the Government be able to provide an update on the status of these cross-border discussions and whether they are progressing as expected, and aligned with our infrastructure plans and timelines?

sections.label: Singapore 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution
sections.summary: Singapore submitted its 2035 NDC to the UNFCCC, committing to emissions of 45 to 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, Singapore submitted our 2035 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We are among just 13 countries to do so on time, out of a total of 195 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We have committed to reducing our emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: It builds on our previous target to peak and then reduce emissions to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Forty-five million tonnes keeps us on a straight-line trajectory from 60 million tonnes in 2030 down to net zero by 2050, aligning with the goals of the Paris Agreement.

sections.label: Solar deployment goal achieved
sections.summary: At the end of last year, Singapore achieved its goal of 1.5 gigawatts-peak of solar deployment by 2025, ahead of schedule and more than triple 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Despite our limited land area, we have pushed hard on solar, which remains our most viable domestic source of renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that at the end of last year, we achieved our goal of 1.5 gigawatts-peak of solar deployment by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This is ahead of schedule and more than triple where we were in 2020.

sections.label: Carbon tax trajectory
sections.summary: The current trajectory is to progressively increase the carbon tax to $45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027, with a view to $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Our current trajectory is to progressively increase the carbon tax to $45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027, with a view to reaching $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Electricity imports and carbon credits
sections.summary: Singapore increased its indicative need for electricity imports from four to eight gigawatts by 2035 and awarded conditional regulatory approvals for 5.6 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Miss Chan asked about our collaborations on electricity imports and carbon credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We recently increased our indicative need for electricity imports from four gigawatts to eight gigawatts   by 2035 and have awarded conditional regulatory approvals to potential partners in Indonesia, Vietnam and Cambodia for 5.6 gigawatts of low-carbon electricity imports.

sections.label: Sustainable fuel uplift for flights
sections.summary: From next year, all flights departing Singapore must have a 1% sustainable fuel uplift, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: From next year, all flights departing Singapore will be required to have a 1% uplift of sustainable fuel, with the goal to raise this to 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund top-up
sections.summary: Singapore is topping up $5 billion to the Future Energy Fund to make critical infrastructure investments and support suitable solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In this transition to a low-carbon future, we will have to explore multiple, sometimes overlapping pathways so that we can find the right mix for ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: This is why we are topping up $5 billion to the Future Energy Fund to make critical infrastructure investments and support solutions that are the most appropriate for us.

sections.label: Global offshore wind market growth
sections.summary: The global offshore wind market is expected to grow to US$126 billion per annum by 2030, and Cyan Renewables is a new local company set up in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The global offshore wind market is expected to grow to US$126 billion per annum by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Cyan Renewables is a new local company set up in 2022.

sections.label: Singapore sustainable aviation fuel production
sections.summary: Singapore is one of the world's leading producers of sustainable aviation fuels, emits 0.1% of global emissions but is affected by 100% of emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Singapore is also one of the world's leading producers today of sustainable aviation fuels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: While we have a broad suite of plans to get ourselves to net-zero, keeping global warming below 1.5°C will depend on other countries doing their part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We emit 0.1% of the world's global emissions but we are affected by 100% of the emissions.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: Singapore is putting aside $5 billion in this Budget to top-up the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund, expecting rising sea levels to require about $100 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: As a low-lying island nation, we must therefore prepare for the reality of rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We are starting now and expect this will require something in the order of $100 billion in the coming decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We are putting aside $5 billion in this Budget to top-up the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

sections.label: Petrochemical plants emissions efficiency
sections.summary: Singapore intends to keep its petrochemical plants in the top quartile of emissions efficiency and has one of the largest sustainable aviation fuel facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On industrial sectors and how we approach that, there has been a plan on what we intend to do there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And what our intention is, is to make sure that our petrochemical plants in Singapore always are in the top quartile of emissions efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And as I mentioned, we are not just talking about the traditional petrochemical plants anymore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We actually have one of the largest, if not, the largest sustainable aviation fuel facilities in the world in Singapore, which has recently expanded as well.

sections.label: Carbon border adjustment taxes
sections.summary: The speaker says carbon border adjustment taxes are in early days but are a reason for Singapore's own carbon tax and measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: It is something which is in the early days, and they are working on it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But we do have to take into cognisance carbon border adjustment taxes, and that is another reason why we need to put in our own measures and our own carbon tax and other measures in Singapore.

sections.label: Carbon tax increase after 2030
sections.summary: The speaker says the carbon tax is being increased from $25 to beyond that in 2030 and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Yes, Mr Chairman, that is why we have indicated when we are increasing from $25 to beyond that in 2030, and then beyond that.

sections.label: NTUC survey on raising children
sections.summary: An NTUC survey of over 1,000 married individuals found less than half of parents found the financial requirements of raising children manageable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: While flexible work arrangements and the introduction of Shared Parental Leave have helped alleviate some stresses related to managing work and family commitments, in a recent survey by the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) of more than 1,000 married individuals, less than half of parents surveyed found the financial requirements of raising children manageable.

sections.label: Singapore total fertility rate 2023
sections.summary: Singapore's total fertility rate reached an all-time low in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore's total fertility rate (TFR) reached an all-time low in 2023.

sections.label: Israel TFR and age dependency
sections.summary: Israel's TFR stayed relatively stable at 2.85 births per woman in 2023, while Singapore's age dependency ratio was 33% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While major urban and developed nations and cities have all seen declining TFR over the past years, Israel's TRF has remained relatively stable over the past decade, with a slight decrease to 2.85 births per woman in 2023, despite high inflation and a high cost of living also being a problem for that country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the World Bank, Singapore's age dependency ratio for the dependent population is reported as 33% in 2023.

sections.label: Visit passes for overseas grandparents
sections.summary: The speaker urges parenthood support visit passes of at least three years for parents of foreign spouses, funded by a CPF ParentCare Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Transnational couples, especially, contend with less familial support with one spouse's parents overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to facilitate the visit passes of parents of foreign spouses, so that transnational couples can have better access to familial support during pregnancy and for the first three years of a child's life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There should be a category of visit passes for parenthood support for at least three years, so that overseas grandparents can be present to support the new parents while they find their footing as a new family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To mitigate this, we can require mandatory savings be put aside in one's Central Provident Fund (CPF) account as a "ParentCare Fund", for those who wish to renew their foreign parents or in-laws' visit passes past the grandchild's third birthday.

sections.label: Extending childcare leave recognition
sections.summary: Asks when recognition might be extended to the increased childcare burden, namely childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When might this be extended to recognising the increased childcare burden, that is, childcare leave?

sections.label: Increase Government-Paid Childcare Leave
sections.summary: Proposes raising Government-Paid Childcare Leave from six to eight days for all parents, regardless of number of young children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: My suggestion is to increase our Government-Paid Childcare Leave from six to eight days, to align with the eight days of annual centre closure that the Early Childhood Development Agency allows childcare operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, we should really try to support our young parents to make full use of these opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And this increase to eight days of childcare leave should apply to all parents, regardless of the number of young children they have.

sections.label: Flexibility for parents with more children
sections.summary: Says the crux for parents with more young children is flexibility to balance work and ad hoc childcare demands, not leave entitlement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: As for supporting parents with more young children, I think the crux is actually the amount of flexibility that parents have today to balance work and ad hoc childcare demands as they arise, rather than the adequacy of leave entitlement per se.

sections.label: Unpaid leave for unexpected care needs
sections.summary: Recalls calling to extend parental leave for multiples and pre-term births, and the Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I spoke up calling to extend parental leave for parents with birth of multiples and of pre-term babies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad the Government responded positively and introduced The Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs offering up to four weeks of unpaid leave for parents with births of multiples and of pre-term babies.

sections.label: Older Singaporeans having children
sections.summary: Notes her passed Motion raised older parenthood as a concern, meaning more couples may face difficulties conceiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Chairman, in my Motion titled "Supporting Singaporeans in Starting and Raising Families" that was debated and passed in this House last month, the issue of Singaporeans having children when they are older was one of the concerns raised as this means more couples would likely face increased difficulties in conceiving.

sections.label: More fertility support measures
sections.summary: Asks whether Government will consider upstream fertility education, pre-IVF testing grants, more IVF cycles, private clinic coverage and extended subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Drawing inspiration from these examples, will our Government consider providing even more support with or by: (a) upstream fertility education to help Singaporeans plan their fertility journeys early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Agencies can work with support groups like Fertility Support SG (FSS), who have offered their support by hosting relevant resources and information on their website for easy access, especially by aspiring parents; (b) the introduction of grants for pre-IVF or general fertility testing to help identify issues and allow for appropriate solutioning early, thereby improving the chances of success; (c) expansion of public sector grants to cover more IVF cycles as families may want more than one child or face complex cases that require additional rounds of treatment; and (d) allowing grants to cover the cost of treatments in private clinics as well, giving couples more options, particularly so when time is of the essence in many of such cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Additionally, in specific instances where the woman undergoing treatment is below the age of 40 and the fertility medical team at public hospitals have recommended that she continues treatment beyond her subsidised assisted conception procedure cycles, will the Government consider extending the coverage of subsidies up to the point when the patient successfully conceives or when the fertility medical team advises her to stop?

sections.label: Large Families Scheme limits
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Large Families Scheme but says financial incentives alone will not reverse demographic trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I support the Large Families Scheme, financial incentives alone will not reverse demographic trends.

sections.label: Policies helping large families
sections.summary: The passage proposes school vacancies, enhanced Third Child Priority Scheme for BTO flats, better flat matching, and workplace tax benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Policies should turn large families into an advantage, not a burden.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can: (a) set aside more primary school vacancies for their children; (b) enhance the Third Child Priority Scheme to provide them with more chances to secure the Build-To-Order (BTO) of their choice, including 5-room BTO flats if they wish; and (c) better match flat types with family needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Workplaces can offer tax benefits for employees with three or more children.

sections.label: Gift and fertility rate
sections.summary: The passage calls the approach a step in the right direction but asks whether the gift will move the total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This approach is certainly a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, while the gift is a meaningful gesture, we must ask: will it be enough to move the needle on our total fertility rate?

sections.label: Ageing and low fertility
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore faces an ageing population and low fertility rate, with 30,800 resident births and a 2024 TFR of 0.97.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To ensure that Singapore continues to thrive, we must address two demographic challenges which are also faced by many other societies around the world – a rapidly ageing population and a low fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We also welcomed 30,800 resident births, a slight increase from 30,500 in the previous year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Our preliminary TFR for 2024 was 0.97, unchanged from 2023.

sections.label: Old-age support ratio
sections.summary: The resident old-age support ratio almost halved from six in 2014 to 3.5 in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The resident old-age support ratio has almost halved from six in 2014 to 3.5 in 2024.

sections.label: Shared Parental Leave weeks
sections.summary: After the new Shared Parental Leave is fully implemented next year, parents will have 30 weeks of paid parental leave in the first year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: After the new Shared Parental Leave is fully implemented next year, parents will have 30 weeks of paid parental leave to care for their infants in the first year after birth.

sections.label: Support for large families
sections.summary: Families get $16,000 per third or later child born from 18 February, plus doubled CDA grant and new grants and credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Families will receive an additional $16,000 for each third or subsequent child, born on or after 18 February this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The CDA First Step Grant will be doubled from $5,000 to $10,000, and the families will receive a new Large Family MediSave Grant of $5,000, and $6,000 in Large Family LifeSG Credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Existing large families will receive $1,000 in Large Family LifeSG Credits annually, for each third or subsequent child until the year the child turns six.

sections.label: ART treatment co-funding
sections.summary: Eligible couples can receive up to 75% co-funding for ART treatments for up to three fresh and three frozen cycles at public institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, eligible couples can receive up to 75% in co-funding for ART treatments for up to three fresh and three frozen cycles at public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Pregnancy and parenting support
sections.summary: Expecting couples can access the Parent Hub, and the Child and Maternal Health Strategy provides mental health screenings and antenatal education programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Expecting couples today can access the Health Promotion Board's Parent Hub, a one-stop online portal with health-related resources and tips for their pregnancy and parenting journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy and Action Plan also provides enhanced support for pregnant women and couples, such as the introduction of mental health screenings and support for pregnant women and new fathers at antenatal and postnatal stages at KK Women's and Children's Hospital and National University Hospital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: More antenatal education programmes have also been rolled out at community touchpoints to help couples better prepare themselves for pregnancy, childbirth and parenthood.

sections.label: SG60 Baby Gift
sections.summary: All Singapore-citizen babies born in 2025 will receive a special SG60 Baby Gift to celebrate their birth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister mentioned at the Budget debate, all Singapore-citizen babies born in 2025 will receive a special SG60 Baby Gift to celebrate their birth.

sections.label: SG60 Baby Gift collection
sections.summary: Parents of babies born in 2025 can register online, with distribution at community events in April and May 2025 and home delivery from mid-May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Parents whose babies are born in 2025 will be able to register online for the gift.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We will launch the distribution of the gift at various community events in April and May 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For those who are unable to collect the gift at these events, or who register for the SG60 Baby Gift after 15 March 2025, we will arrange for the gift to be delivered to your homes from mid-May 2025.

sections.label: New citizenships granted in 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, about 24,000 new citizenships were granted, including 1,400 to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In 2024, we granted about 24,000 new citizenships, including 1,400 to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sections.label: TFR target proposal
sections.summary: A former public and civil servant asks whether the Prime Minister's Office would set a TFR target of 1.0 in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: But having been a public and civil servant myself for almost 20 years before I stepped into a political role, I know well the culture of what gets measured, gets attention, gets resources and gets done.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: So, I am wondering whether the Prime Minister's Office is open to setting a TFR target of bringing it back to 1.0 in the next five years.

sections.label: Addressing concerns on measures
sections.summary: The passage lists concerns to be addressed through enhanced Baby Bonus, enhanced CDA, housing, a new classification framework and Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs.

sentences.text: Let us see how we can address each of these concerns, whether it is through enhanced Baby Bonus; enhanced CDA; or with housing, apart from ramping up, also the new classification framework; the Tripartite Guidelines on FWAs.

sections.label: Baby remark and import correction
sections.summary: The speaker says having a baby is not a homework assignment and corrects green electricity import need from four to six gigawatts.

sentences.text: It is not like a homework assignment to have a baby.

sentences.speaker: ﻿Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I had indicated that we are increasing our indicative need for green electricity imports from four to eight gigawatts.

sentences.speaker: ﻿Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I meant to say, "four to six gigawatts".

sections.label: Equity Market Development Programme launch
sections.summary: On the launch of the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme addressing demand issues, the speaker says it is better than nothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On the launch of the $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme ddressing demand issues, it is a case of better than nothing.

sections.label: Five billion small fraction
sections.summary: The passage states that $5 billion is a small fraction of the free-float market capitalisation of the Singapore market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the grand scheme of things, $5 billion is just a small fraction of the free-float market capitalisation of the Singapore market.

sections.label: Urging government-linked listings
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government, via its investment entities, to lead in having its companies list on the Singapore Exchange.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While MAS has taken the lead on the demand side with the Equity Market Development Programme, on the supply side, I urge the Government, via its investment entities, to similarly take the lead for its companies to list on the Singapore Exchange (SGX).

sections.label: Stake via company listings
sections.summary: The scheme worked well, and the current generation can get a stake through an IPO of private companies held by Temasek listed on the Singapore exchange.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For all intents and purposes, the scheme worked well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can give this current generation of Singaporeans a stake in the country via a meaningful Initial Public Offering (IPO) of the next wave of various private companies held by Temasek and encouraging them to list on the Singapore exchange.

sections.label: Ex-offender bank account access
sections.summary: The MP seeks an update on banks offering Limited Purpose Bank Accounts for ex-offenders and MAS data on take-up, citing a constituent rejected by six banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In response to a cut filed in 2022 by my colleague, Mr Gerald Giam, then-Deputy Chairman of MAS Mr Lawrence Wong had spoken on the Limited Purpose Bank Accounts, which was then in its pilot phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These accounts are meant to help ex-offenders to access basic banking services, including receiving their salaries and Government payouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I seek an update on how many local banks are offering such accounts for ex-offenders and whether MAS has data on the take-up rate for such accounts by ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My constituent is an ex-offender and needed a bank account in order to receive her salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I sent appeals to six different local banks, which were all unsuccessful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MAS offered to forward my constituent's appeal to DBS, UOB and OCBC but stated they were unable to compel any banks to open an account for my constituent.

sections.label: Equity Market Development Programme launch
sections.summary: Measures were introduced to increase investor interest and deepen trading liquidity, including a $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: On demand side, we introduced measures to increase investor interest and deepen trading liquidity, such as the launch of a $5 billion Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP).

sections.label: Banks offering limited purpose accounts
sections.summary: MAS does not prohibit banks from opening accounts for ex-offenders, and from January 2022 to June 2024 banks offered more than 3,600 LPBAs.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS does not prohibit banks from opening accounts for ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: However, banks may choose to offer accounts with more limited functions to ex-offenders of financial crimes to manage the higher risk of them being misused.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: From January 2022 to June 2024, banks have offered more than 3,600 LPBAs.

sections.label: Rejected appeal for ex-offender
sections.summary: A resident convicted of money laundering had her bank appeal rejected because her account is under a seizure order and documents were not provided.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Mr Faisal Manap's resident was convicted of money laundering offences and sentenced to 20 months' jail.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The banks have rejected the appeal because the appellant's bank account is still subject to a seizure order, and she has not provided the necessary information and supporting documents to the banks.

sentences.speaker: ﻿The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MAS will continue to work with the banks to see if more can be done to help the appellant.

sections.label: Sustained funding for equities market
sections.summary: The MP asked whether there will be sustained funding and cash injections for continued support of the equities market over the medium- to long-term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: Specific to the Equity Market Development Programme, I asked whether there will be sustained funding and cash injections for continued support of the equities market over the medium- to long-term.

sections.label: Local equities market fund focus
sections.summary: MAS wants funds to focus on the local equities market, including mid-caps and smaller companies, not just index stocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As to the specifics of how we design it, I think MAS has explained it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We do want to set a focus on the local equities market, for these funds to focus on the local equities market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Not to just invest in the index stocks, because those are already quite well-researched and well-traded, but to look for opportunities in other stocks as well – the mid-caps and the smaller companies with potential.

sections.label: EBRC directions on GRCs and SMCs
sections.summary: Past EBRCs reduced average GRC size or increased SMCs, but this time the Prime Minister directed keeping GRC size, SMC proportion and elector-to-MP ratio about the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: In the past three General Elections in 2020, 2015 and 2011, EBRCs were directed to reduce the average size of Group Representation Constituencies (GRCs) and/or to increase the number of SMCs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: This time, the Prime Minister directed that the EBRC "should seek to keep the average size of GRCs, the proportion of Members of Parliament (MPs) elected from SMCs and the average ratio of electors to elected MPs, all at about the same as that in the last General Election".

sections.label: Grants of ₣50,000 to ₣100,000
sections.summary: Grants of ₣50,000 to ₣100,000 are given over six to 12 months to allow room to fail fast and pivot quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Grants of ₣50,000 to ₣100,000 are given over a six- to 12-month timespan to allow room to fail fast and pivot quickly.

sections.label: Singapore quantum research funding and MAS
sections.summary: Last year Singapore made available nearly $400 million to quantum research, with MAS promoting quantum key distribution for banking.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore made available nearly $400 million to quantum research, with MAS promoting quantum key distribution (QKD) for the banking sector.

sections.label: Industry move to fault-tolerant quantum computing
sections.summary: The industry is moving toward fault-tolerant quantum computing, as shown by Google's December 2024 Willow chip and Microsoft's 2025 Majorana 1 processor.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Yet, the industry is moving toward fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC), as illustrated by Google's December 2024 Willow chip demonstrating exponentially decreasing errors as qubits increase and Microsoft's 2025 Majorana 1 processor aiming for a million qubits on one chip.

sections.label: US post-quantum encryption standards
sections.summary: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology recently finalised post-quantum standards that function like current public-key encryption and are expected to be adopted universally.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology recently finalised post-quantum standards, which function like current public-key encryption and are expected to be adopted universally.

sections.label: Overseas exposure for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Government says more Singaporeans need overseas exposure for global leadership roles, with initiatives like iPOST and OMIP for overseas postings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For the private sector, the Government has stated that more Singaporeans need overseas exposure to take on leadership roles in global firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And to achieve that, there are initiatives, such as the Institute of Banking and Finance's International Postings Programme (iPOST) and Workforce Singapore's Overseas Markets Immersion Programme (OMIP) for financial institutions and employers to send their workers for overseas exposure.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: With Singapore becoming a super-aged society, retirement and re-employment ages rise to 64 and 69 in 2026, with the Public Service acting from 1 July 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Singaporeans are living longer and we will soon become a super-aged society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the face of these demographic changes, the Government has announced that the retirement and re-employment ages would be raised to 64 and 69 respectively in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To support officers who wish to continue serving Singapore and Singaporeans, the Public Service announced that it would take the lead to raise the retirement and re-employment ages to 64 and 69 respectively from 1 July 2025, one year ahead of the national timeline.

sections.label: Assessing R&D over long term
sections.summary: R&D is a long-cycle endeavour whose payoffs are more appropriately assessed over the long-term rather than the short-term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Chair, R&D is a long-cycle endeavour and any payoffs will be more appropriately assessed over the long-term, rather than the short-term, as Ms He has suggested.

sections.label: National Research Foundation portfolio approach
sections.summary: The National Research Foundation takes a portfolio approach, supporting R&D across fields and maturity levels with relevant programme management approaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Our National Research Foundation takes a portfolio approach, supporting R&D across fields and at different levels of maturity and applying relevant programme management approaches.

sections.label: Doubling down on quantum research
sections.summary: Quantum research is an example of where initial promise has led to doubling down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Quantum research is an example of where we are doubling down after seeing initial promise.

sections.label: Limit to reducing GRC sizes
sections.summary: There is an asymptotical limit to EBRC reducing average GRC size, and that limit is one, with all electoral divisions being SMCs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Ms Poa will agree that there will be an asymptotical limit to asking EBRC to keep reducing the average size of GRCs and that limit is one, with all electoral divisions being SMCs.

sections.label: Public Service three focus areas
sections.summary: The Public Service will focus on strengthening three areas this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: The Public Service will focus on strengthening three areas this year.

sections.label: Preparing officers for longer careers
sections.summary: A Public Service Career Coach Network was introduced and the CareerFitness programme will be ramped up to help officers build career resilience and agility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: As we prepare our officers for an increasingly complex environment, Mr Patrick Tay asked about our efforts to prepare officers for our expanded or lengthened career spans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We have introduced a Public Service Career Coach Network and will be ramping up our CareerFitness programme to empower officers to build career resilience and agility across different life stages.

sections.label: Coordinated citizen-centric service delivery
sections.summary: In response to Mr Yip Hon Weng's question, service delivery will continue to be integrated from a citizen-centric rather than silo-Ministry perspective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Second, in response to Mr Yip Hon Weng's question on coordinated citizen services, we will continue to integrate our service delivery from a citizen-centric perspective, rather than a silo-Ministry perspective.

sections.label: Civil Service College building leadership teams
sections.summary: The Civil Service College will help agencies build stronger, more agile leadership teams, and three things must be focused on urgently this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: To this end, our Civil Service College will lean forward to help different agencies to build stronger and more agile leadership teams to bring out the best in our agencies to enable Singapore and Singaporean success.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, three things that we need to do and we will need to focus on them urgently this year.

sections.label: Citizen services and building teams
sections.summary: Efforts will continue to build services around the citizen for a seamless experience, and teams will be built to have different perspectives for robust solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Two, we will continue to focus our efforts to build our services around the citizen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We aim for a more seamless service experience for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And third, beyond building the individual, we must build our teams to have different perspectives, to be able to see things from different angles, so that we can have more robust solutions.

sections.label: Overcoming challenges and political partnership
sections.summary: Success requires a strong, continuous partnership between political leadership and the Public Service, letting it execute with consistency and conviction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Only then, can we be more assured that we are able to overcome tomorrow's challenges, seize new opportunities to benefit all Singaporeans and be a Public Service that can continue to be the pride of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: But to be successful, we must maintain a strong, continuous and consistent partnership between the political leadership and the Public Service, that allows our Public Service to execute with consistency and conviction, without fear or favour.

sections.label: EBRC GRC SMC conditions
sections.summary: The Minister is asked to explain why imposing conditions on GRC and SMC sizes is acceptable while requiring EBRC to explain its changes is considered overimposing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Can the Minister explain the logic behind this position that it is okay to impose or to specify to EBRC that the average size of GRCs and the proportion of SMCs should be maintained at current levels, but it is overimposing on EBRC to ask them to explain the reasons for their changes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Because according to normal logic, it would actually be the other way round, that you do not impose conditions on the sizes of GRCs or the number of SMCs if you want to preserve the independence of EBRC, but simply require them to explain the reasons behind their decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Chair, I am quite sure EBRC will explain its thinking in due course.
